judgments.description: One judgment per provision id listed in the document, in the order given.

clause_id.description: The provision id, copied exactly from the square brackets.

issues.description: Every construction issue this provision carries, one entry each, with its own probability. Only defects you can NAME go in the list -- but if you can name one, list it however unsure you are, with a LOW probability (0.05, 0.10, 0.20). Uncertainty goes into the probability; the empty list is only for a provision you looked at and found nothing to name in. The question deciding between them is not whether you are confident but whether you can say what is wrong. Ask about both types before moving on: a provision can carry a defect in its own words AND sit badly against another one, and where you can name both, list both -- the second entry is held to the same standard as the first, not a higher one. A type with no entry is read as probability 0, which is what it means: nothing specific was found.

issue.description: Two sentences naming THIS specific defect: for risk type 1 the ambiguous term or the general-vs-specific tension; for risk type 2 the other provision it cannot be squared with, named. Never empty and never null -- an entry exists only because there is a defect to name. If you cannot name one, write no entry.

type.description: 1 if the trouble is INSIDE this provision's own words -- a word that can be read more than one way, a writing mistake, a general term whose reach against its own list is unclear -- however many cross-references, or documents mounted beside this one, it took to notice. 2 if the trouble is in HOW THIS PROVISION STANDS WITH ANOTHER PART of the instrument: the two cannot both be given effect, or what this one means only settles once they are read together, or a recital pulls against operative words. Type 2 is not only direct conflict. How you came to notice a defect does not decide its type -- citing another provision, or another document, as evidence of what a word here means is still type 1.

prob.description: Probability in (0, 1] that a court would have something to construe on account of THIS issue. Greater than zero: the entry exists because the defect does, and a defect you would put at 0 is one you should not have listed. Low values are expected and are where most named issues belong -- 0.08 or 0.15 on a defect you can name but would not bet on is the right answer, not a reason to omit the entry. Two decimal places, on a 0.01 grid (0.03, 0.17, 0.62) -- do not round to the nearest 0.05 or 0.1. The range is stated here and not as minimum/maximum, which structured output rejects on a number; the reader clamps it.
